metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Audit Map (Batch 6)
metadata.methodology: Five-Phase Static Analysis with Counterexample Construction

audit_entries.title: Verify stealth address generation is cryptographically secure

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: The burn_address.rs circuit uses poseidon3(domain, recipient, secret) where domain is a fixed 4-byte constant 'burn'. The compute_burn_address_from_secret function validates POW_DIFFICULTY leading zero bits before returning. No input validation bypass found - all inputs flow through Poseidon hash.
Stealth address generation is stateless - it's a pure cryptographic function with no state transitions to violate.
The find_pow_nonce function iterates from 0u64 to find a valid nonce. While this is O(2^POW_DIFFICULTY) in expectation, it's client-side computation. No on-chain resource exhaustion risk.
BurnAddressError::PowDifficultyUnsatisfied is returned when PoW constraint not met. The error is properly propagated. No silent failures.
Stealth address generation is deterministic and client-side. Same (recipient, secret) always produces same address. No race condition possible.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker attempts to predict stealth address without knowing the user's secret by brute-forcing the Poseidon preimage.
attack_path: 1. Attacker observes stealth address on-chain
2. Attacker attempts to find (recipient, secret) pair that hashes to observed address
3. Must also satisfy PoW constraint (POW_DIFFICULTY leading zeros)
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - Poseidon preimage resistance with ~128-bit security prevents finding the secret. Even with known recipient, the secret provides sufficient entropy. Note: burn address collision resistance is 89-bit due to ADDRESS_BIT_LENGTH truncation (known issue, out of scope per docs).

guards_found.description: Poseidon hash function provides collision resistance and preimage resistance
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Poseidon3 is a well-audited hash function

guards_found.description: POW_DIFFICULTY leading zero bits required, adding enumeration cost
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Adds computational cost to address enumeration

guards_found.description: burn_address_var enforces PoW constraint in ZK circuit
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - On-chain verification matches off-chain generation

phase5_confidence.rationale: Stealth address generation relies on well-established cryptographic primitives (Poseidon hash). The implementation correctly uses domain separation, validates PoW constraints, and provides consistent behavior between native and circuit implementations. The 89-bit collision resistance is a known limitation documented in the codebase.

audit_entries.title: Verify Nova IVC proof generation validates secret-to-address binding

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: The Nova circuit must constrain that the claimed recipient address matches hash(domain, recipient, secret). The burn_address_var function in zkp/src/circuits/burn_address.rs:87-110 enforces this constraint in the circuit.
IVC proof generation is off-chain client-side computation. On-chain verification validates the proof independently.
Proof generation is client-side. Resource exhaustion is not an on-chain concern.
On-chain, invalid proofs cause revert with InvalidProof() error. The verification is not silent.
Proof generation is deterministic. The same inputs always produce the same proof (excluding any randomness in the ZK scheme which doesn't affect soundness).

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker generates IVC proof for transfers they don't own (transfers to addresses not derived from their secret).
attack_path: 1. Attacker observes transfers to stealth address A on-chain
2. Attacker attempts to generate IVC proof claiming ownership of those transfers
3. Proof must satisfy circuit constraint: burn_address = poseidon(domain, recipient, secret)
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - The circuit constraint burn_address_var enforces that the provided secret must hash (with the recipient) to the claimed burn address. Without knowing the original secret, attacker cannot produce a valid proof.

guards_found.description: burn_address_var enforces secret-to-address binding via Poseidon hash
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Cryptographic binding in ZK circuit
EFFECTIVE - On-chain verification rejects invalid proofs

phase5_confidence.rationale: The Nova circuit enforces secret-to-address binding through cryptographic constraints. The sonobe/folding-schemes library is marked as TRUSTED in the trust model. On-chain verification through IRootDecider ensures only valid proofs are accepted.

audit_entries.title: Verify STATE-USER-HAS-NOVA-PROOF implies valid IVC proof ownership

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: On-chain verification validates proof structure and cryptographic soundness. The proof decoding and verification happens atomically.
The STATE-USER-HAS-NOVA-PROOF is a client-side state. On-chain, the proof is verified at submission time (teleport). No persistent on-chain state tracks proof possession.
Proof submission costs gas. Invalid proofs revert early, limiting gas consumption.
InvalidProof() error is thrown for invalid proofs. Other specific errors for invalid public inputs.
Proof possession is client-side. On-chain verification is stateless per-call.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker attempts to submit a proof generated by another user for their transfers.
attack_path: 1. User A generates valid IVC proof for their transfers
2. Attacker B intercepts or observes the proof (front-running)
3. Attacker B submits the proof claiming ownership
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - The proof public inputs include recipient hash (gr.hash()) which binds to the caller's address via GeneralRecipient. The _teleport function verifies: require(recipient == gr.hash()) where gr includes the recipient address. Front-runner cannot claim tokens for User A.

guards_found.description: Proof public inputs include recipient hash binding proof to owner
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Cryptographic binding prevents proof theft

guards_found.description: GeneralRecipient includes chainId, preventing cross-chain replay
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Chain-specific proofs

phase5_confidence.rationale: The proof public inputs cryptographically bind the proof to the recipient address and chain ID. Front-running and proof theft are prevented by these bindings verified on-chain.

audit_entries.title: Verify verifier rotation restricted to owner during emergency

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: setVerifiers function validates all addresses are non-zero. Protected by onlyOwner modifier.

The setVerifiers function can be called at any time by owner, NOT only during emergency. This differs from the checklist expectation. However, this is marked OUT_OF_SCOPE per trust model (owner operations trusted).
Fixed gas cost operation. No loop or unbounded computation.
ZeroAddress() error for invalid inputs. No silent failures.
Single storage write operation. No race condition possible.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Non-owner attempts to rotate verifiers to accept malicious proofs.
attack_path: 1. Attacker identifies malicious verifier contracts that accept all proofs
2. Attacker calls setVerifiers() to install malicious verifiers
3. Attacker submits forged proofs that pass verification
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - onlyOwner modifier prevents non-owner from calling setVerifiers(). Owner is trusted per trust model.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Only owner can rotate verifiers

guards_found.description: All five verifier addresses validated as non-zero
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Prevents setting zero addresses

phase5_confidence.rationale: The setVerifiers function is properly protected by onlyOwner. Note: The function can be called outside emergency state, but owner operations are OUT_OF_SCOPE per trust model.

audit_entries.title: Verify emergency deactivation requires prior verifier rotation

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: deactivateEmergency() has no parameters to validate. It calls _unpause().

IMPORTANT FINDING: deactivateEmergency() does NOT require prior verifier rotation. It only calls _unpause() and emits DeactivateEmergency. The checklist expectation of 'prior rotation required' is NOT enforced in code.
Fixed gas cost operation.
No custom errors. Relies on Pausable's whenPaused if needed (but not used here).
Single state transition. No race condition.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Owner deactivates emergency without rotating compromised verifiers.
attack_path: 1. Emergency triggered due to divergent proofs (compromised verifier)
2. Owner calls deactivateEmergency() without calling setVerifiers()
3. Compromised verifier remains active, allowing continued exploitation
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: NOT BLOCKED - The code does not enforce verifier rotation before emergency deactivation. However, this is marked OUT_OF_SCOPE per trust model (owner operations trusted). Owner is responsible for proper recovery procedure.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE for access control, but does not enforce rotation prerequisite

phase3_guard_search.missing_guard: No check that verifiers were rotated before deactivation

phase5_confidence.rationale: The code does not enforce verifier rotation before emergency deactivation. This relies on owner following correct operational procedure. Marked OUT_OF_SCOPE per trust model since owner operations are trusted.

audit_entries.title: Verify STATE-EMERGENCY-RECOVERED implies new verifiers active

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: Recovery state is implied after owner calls deactivateEmergency(). New verifiers are only active if setVerifiers() was called beforehand.
The STATE-EMERGENCY-RECOVERED is a logical state, not explicitly tracked on-chain. It's implied by paused=false after emergency.
Fixed gas cost operations.
Normal operations resume after _unpause(). Functions with whenNotPaused become callable.
No race condition. State transitions are atomic.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: System returns to normal operation with old (compromised) verifiers still active.
attack_path: 1. Emergency triggered
2. Owner calls deactivateEmergency() without setVerifiers()
3. Old verifiers remain active
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: POSSIBLE - The code does not enforce new verifiers. However, owner is trusted per trust model to follow correct procedure.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Emergency blocks operations until owner deactivates

phase3_guard_search.missing_guard: No on-chain enforcement that new verifiers are set during recovery

phase5_confidence.rationale: Recovery state relies on owner following correct operational procedure. Owner is trusted per trust model. On-chain code does not enforce verifier rotation as part of recovery.

audit_entries.title: Verify reward calculation uses correct IncentiveLib parameters

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: The _wrap function reads feeParams from storage atomically and passes to IncentiveLib. Parameters validated at setFeeParams time via validateFeeParams().
Reward calculation uses pre-deposit liquidity (liquidityBefore) to prevent manipulation by the deposit itself affecting the reward rate.
IncentiveLib uses O(1) arithmetic operations. No unbounded loops.
IncentiveLib returns 0 for edge cases (T=0, amount=0, overflow scenarios) rather than reverting.
ReentrancyGuardTransient prevents reentrancy. Parameters read from storage in same transaction.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker manipulates liquidity between parameter read and reward calculation.
attack_path: 1. Attacker deposits in same block as victim
2. Attempts to change liquidity mid-calculation
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - liquidityBefore is computed from balanceBefore which is captured at function start. The reward calculation uses this snapshot, not current balance.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Prevents mid-transaction manipulation
EFFECTIVE - ReentrancyGuardTransient is robust

guards_found.description: Reward uses floor division protecting protocol
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Never overpays rewards

phase5_confidence.rationale: Reward calculation correctly uses pre-deposit liquidity snapshot, is protected by reentrancy guard, and uses floor rounding to protect the protocol.

audit_entries.title: Verify SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom used for token pulls

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: For ERC20 tokens, UNDERLYING_TOKEN.safeTransferFrom is used. For native ETH, msg.value validation is used.
Transfer happens before minting. If transfer fails, entire transaction reverts.
Single transfer operation. No unbounded computation.
SafeERC20 reverts on transfer failure. Additional check: if (received == 0) revert UnderlyingPullFailed()
Protected by nonReentrant. No race condition possible.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker uses malicious ERC20 token that returns false on transfer but doesn't revert.
attack_path: 1. Attacker deploys malicious ERC20 that returns false on transferFrom
2. LiquidityManager calls transferFrom
3. Token returns false, no actual transfer happens
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom handles non-standard ERC20 tokens by checking return value and reverting if false or no return. Additionally, received amount check ensures actual balance increase.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Handles non-standard ERC20 return values
EFFECTIVE - Double-checks transfer success
EFFECTIVE - Catches edge cases

phase5_confidence.rationale: SafeERC20 is correctly imported and used. Additional balance verification provides defense-in-depth. Non-standard ERC20 tokens are properly handled.

audit_entries.title: Verify minting exact (amount + reward) to user

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: amountOut = received + reward is computed. ZERC20_TOKEN.mint(receiver, amountOut) mints exactly this amount.
Mint happens after liquidity pull. Order is correct: pull -> calculate reward -> mint.
Single mint operation. No unbounded computation.
If mint fails (e.g., ValueTooLarge), entire transaction reverts.
Protected by nonReentrant. No reentrancy possible.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker attempts to receive more zERC20 than deposited + legitimate reward.
attack_path: 1. Attacker deposits X underlying
2. Expects to receive > X + IncentiveLib reward
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - amountOut is computed deterministically as received + reward. No path to inflate this value. received is validated against actual balance change.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - No rounding error in addition
EFFECTIVE - Prevents burning to zero address

phase5_confidence.rationale: Mint amount is computed as exact sum of received deposit and calculated reward. No overflow risk due to 248-bit constraint on zERC20 values.

audit_entries.title: Verify Wrapped event emitted with accurate parameters

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: Event parameters (msg.sender, receiver, amountOut, reward) are populated from transaction state, not user input.
Event emitted after mint. CEI pattern followed: transfer -> mint -> emit.
Single event emission. No unbounded computation.
Event is always emitted on successful wrap. No conditional emission.
Event emission is atomic with state changes in same transaction.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Event parameters don't match actual transaction values.
attack_path: 1. User wraps X underlying
2. Event reports different values than actual state changes
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - Event parameters directly reference computed variables: msg.sender (caller), receiver (param), amountOut (computed), reward (computed). All values are from the same execution context.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - No separate event data path

phase5_confidence.rationale: Event parameters directly reference transaction state variables. No discrepancy possible between event and actual state.

audit_entries.title: Verify user balance increased by minted amount

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: zERC20.mint() is called via ZERC20_TOKEN.mint(receiver, amountOut). The receiver address is validated earlier.
OpenZeppelin ERC20Upgradeable._mint atomically updates balance and totalSupply.
Single state update. O(1) operation.
zERC20._update reverts if value > type(uint248).max with ValueTooLarge error.
Protected by nonReentrant at LiquidityManager level. Mint is atomic.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: User's balance doesn't increase by the minted amount.
attack_path: 1. LiquidityManager calls zERC20.mint(receiver, amountOut)
2. receiver's balance doesn't increase by amountOut
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - OpenZeppelin's ERC20._mint directly adds to _balances[account]. This is an atomic operation. The only path to not increasing balance is revert, which fails the entire wrap transaction.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Battle-tested implementation
EFFECTIVE - Prevents overflow and ZK incompatibility

phase5_confidence.rationale: OpenZeppelin's ERC20 implementation guarantees atomic balance updates. zERC20 inherits this implementation and adds additional constraints but doesn't break the balance update logic.

audit_entries.title: Verify fee calculation uses ceiling division

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: Fee calculation uses _ceilDiv helper which implements ceiling division correctly.
Fee is calculated before burn. Order is: calculate fee -> burn zERC20 -> transfer underlying.
O(1) arithmetic operations.
_ceilDiv returns 0 for a=0 case, correctly handles edge cases.
Protected by nonReentrant. No reentrancy during fee calculation.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Attacker exploits floor division to pay less fee than expected.
attack_path: 1. Attacker unwraps amount where fee calculation has remainder
2. With floor division, fee would be rounded down
3. Protocol loses the fractional fee
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - IncentiveLib explicitly uses _ceilDiv: 'return r == 0 ? q : q + 1'. This ensures fee is always rounded UP, protecting the protocol.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Proper ceiling division implementation
EFFECTIVE - Intent is clear and implementation matches

phase5_confidence.rationale: The _ceilDiv function correctly implements ceiling division: if a % b != 0, returns q + 1. This protects the protocol from rounding exploitation on fees.

audit_entries.title: Verify exact unwrap amount burned from user

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: ZERC20_TOKEN.burn(msg.sender, amount) burns the exact unwrap request amount.
Burn happens BEFORE underlying transfer. CEI pattern: burn -> transfer underlying.
Single burn operation. O(1).
If user has insufficient balance, ERC20._burn reverts with ERC20InsufficientBalance error.
Protected by nonReentrant. No reentrancy possible.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: User unwraps but less than requested amount is burned.
attack_path: 1. User calls unwrap(X)
2. Less than X is burned from user's balance
3. User receives underlying but keeps zERC20
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - ZERC20_TOKEN.burn(msg.sender, amount) uses the exact input parameter. OpenZeppelin's _burn directly subtracts from balance. No path to partial burn.

guards_found.description: burn(msg.sender, amount) uses exact input parameter
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - No modification of burn amount
EFFECTIVE - Only LiquidityManager can burn

phase5_confidence.rationale: Burn amount is exactly the unwrap request parameter. No modification or rounding of burn amount. OpenZeppelin implementation is trusted.

audit_entries.title: Verify LiquidityManager transfers exact (amount - fee) using SafeERC20

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: amountOut = amount - feeAmount is computed. SafeERC20.safeTransfer used for ERC20, native ETH uses call with value.
Transfer happens after burn. Order: burn zERC20 -> transfer underlying -> update feeSurplus.
Single transfer operation. O(1).
SafeERC20.safeTransfer reverts on failure. Native ETH transfer checks success flag.
Protected by nonReentrant. Transfer to receiver could be malicious contract but burn already happened.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: User receives more underlying than (amount - fee).
attack_path: 1. User unwraps X zERC20
2. Fee calculated as F
3. User receives more than X - F underlying
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - amountOut = amount - feeAmount is computed directly. SafeERC20.safeTransfer(receiver, amountOut) uses this exact value. No path to inflate transfer amount.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Handles non-standard ERC20
EFFECTIVE - Prevents transfer of unavailable funds
EFFECTIVE - Handles failed native transfers

phase5_confidence.rationale: Transfer amount is exact (amount - fee). SafeERC20 handles non-standard tokens. Liquidity check prevents failed transfers.

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: Event parameters (msg.sender, receiver, amountOut, feeAmount) directly reference transaction state.
Event emitted after all state changes. CEI pattern followed.

Event always emitted on successful unwrap.
Event emission atomic with state changes.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Event parameters don't match actual unwrap values.
attack_path: 1. User unwraps
2. Event reports different values
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - Event directly uses computed variables: msg.sender, receiver, amountOut, feeAmount. All from same execution context.

guards_found.description: Event parameters reference transaction state directly

audit_entries.title: Verify unwrap handles low liquidity by increasing fee (no revert)

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: IncentiveLib.quoteUnwrapFee handles insufficient liquidity case: when liquidity <= amount, fee is calculated to drain available liquidity.
The design DOES allow unwrap to revert with InsufficientLiquidity if amountOut > available balance. This is different from the checklist expectation.
O(1) operations.
InsufficientLiquidity error is thrown when balance < amountOut, which can happen if liquidity is very low.
Protected by nonReentrant.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: User attempts unwrap when liquidity is insufficient, expecting graceful degradation.
attack_path: 1. Pool has 100 underlying, feeSurplus = 50, available = 50
2. User tries to unwrap 60 zERC20
3. Fee curve calculates high fee, but amountOut still > available
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: FINDING: The checklist states unwrap should NOT revert on low liquidity but increase fee instead. However, the actual implementation CAN revert with InsufficientLiquidity if amountOut > available balance. This is a documentation/design mismatch.

guards_found.description: IncentiveLib increases fee as liquidity decreases
guards_found.effectiveness: PARTIALLY EFFECTIVE - Fee increases but can still result in revert
EFFECTIVE for preventing failed transfers, but contradicts design intent

phase5_confidence.rationale: The checklist claims unwrap never reverts on low liquidity (fee adjustment handles it). However, the code CAN revert with InsufficientLiquidity. This may be intended behavior or a design gap. Needs verification against specification.

finding_details.description: The checklist states 'unwrap does NOT revert on low liquidity - fee adjustment handles it'. However, the actual implementation includes InsufficientLiquidity checks at lines 291 and 295 that CAN cause revert when amountOut exceeds available liquidity.
finding_details.recommendation: Verify this is intended behavior. If unwrap should never revert on low liquidity, the fee curve should be designed to always result in amountOut <= available liquidity.

audit_entries.title: Verify SafeERC20.safeTransfer guarantees user receives tokens

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: SafeERC20.safeTransfer handles non-standard ERC20 return values.
If safeTransfer fails, entire transaction reverts. No partial state.
Single transfer. O(1).
SafeERC20 reverts on failure. Native ETH checks success and reverts with UnderlyingSendFailed.
No try-catch that could swallow transfer failure. Protected by nonReentrant.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Transfer silently fails, user doesn't receive tokens.
attack_path: 1. User unwraps successfully
2. Underlying transfer fails silently
3. User burned zERC20 but didn't receive underlying
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - SafeERC20.safeTransfer reverts on failure, rolling back the entire transaction including the burn. No silent failure path.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Handles non-standard tokens
EFFECTIVE - Handles failed native transfers

phase5_confidence.rationale: SafeERC20 guarantees transfer success or revert. No silent failure path. Burn is reverted if transfer fails.

audit_entries.title: Verify _afterTokenTransfer enforces BN254 constraint on all transfers

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: IMPORTANT: The constraint is in _update, not _afterTokenTransfer. The check is 'if (value > type(uint248).max) revert ValueTooLarge()'. This validates the VALUE being transferred, not the resulting balance.
The check validates transfer VALUE, not recipient BALANCE. Multiple small transfers could accumulate to exceed 2^248-1 in a single account.
O(1) check.
ValueTooLarge() error is properly defined and thrown.
Check happens before state modification (in _update before super._update).

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Accumulate balance beyond 2^248-1 via multiple small transfers.
attack_path: 1. Account A has balance 2^248 - 10
2. Transfer 5 to A (passes: value=5 < 2^248)
3. Transfer another 5 to A (passes: value=5 < 2^248)
4. A now has 2^248, then another transfer of 1 makes 2^248+1
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: POTENTIAL ISSUE: The check validates transfer VALUE, not resulting BALANCE. However, uint256 max (2^256-1) is much larger than 2^248-1, so ERC20 storage can technically hold values > 2^248-1. BUT: this is mitigated by controlling mint sources (LiquidityManager and Verifier) which mint reasonable amounts.

guards_found.effectiveness: PARTIALLY EFFECTIVE - Validates transfer value but not resulting balance

guards_found.description: Only LiquidityManager (minter) and Verifier can mint
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Mint amounts are controlled by protocol logic

phase5_confidence.rationale: The check validates transfer VALUE, not resulting BALANCE. The checklist expects balance validation. In practice, controlled minting sources mitigate this, but the property as stated may not be precisely enforced.

finding_details.description: The checklist expects BN254 constraint enforced on recipient's balance after transfers. The actual implementation checks the transfer VALUE (if value > type(uint248).max), not the resulting BALANCE. This means multiple transfers could theoretically accumulate beyond 2^248-1.
finding_details.recommendation: Verify if balance accumulation beyond 2^248-1 is possible in practice given controlled mint sources. Consider adding balance check if required for ZK circuit compatibility.

audit_entries.title: Verify ValueTooLarge revert triggers correctly

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: Comparison is 'value > type(uint248).max'. type(uint248).max = 2^248 - 1. Correctly uses strict > comparison.
Check happens before super._update call, so revert prevents any state change.
O(1) comparison.
Custom error ValueTooLarge() properly defined.
No race condition - single atomic check.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Transfer value exactly at boundary incorrectly reverts.
attack_path: 1. Transfer value = 2^248 - 1 (MAX_VALUE)
2. Check: value > type(uint248).max
4. Should NOT revert
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: PASS - The comparison is strict >, so value = MAX_VALUE passes. Only value > MAX_VALUE reverts. Boundary behavior is correct.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Correct boundary behavior

guards_found.description: Check before super._update ensures revert prevents state change
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - No partial state on revert

phase5_confidence.rationale: The boundary comparison is correctly implemented with strict > operator. MAX_VALUE transfers succeed, MAX_VALUE+1 reverts.

audit_entries.title: Verify atomic balance updates using OpenZeppelin _transfer

attack_vectors_analyzed.finding: zERC20 inherits from ERC20Upgradeable. _transfer is NOT overridden. Uses OpenZeppelin's implementation.
_update is overridden to add hash chain update and event, but calls super._update which performs atomic balance update.
O(1) balance updates.
OpenZeppelin _update handles insufficient balance with ERC20InsufficientBalance error.
Balance updates are single-transaction atomic operations. No external calls between sender debit and receiver credit in _update.

phase2_counterexample_construction.attempted_counterexample: Sender balance decreases but receiver balance doesn't increase.
attack_path: 1. Transfer X from A to B
2. A's balance decreases by X
3. Revert or failure before B's balance increases
phase2_counterexample_construction.outcome: BLOCKED - OpenZeppelin's _update performs both debit and credit in the same code block without external calls between them. If any part fails, entire transaction reverts.

guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Battle-tested implementation

guards_found.description: No external calls between balance updates in _update
guards_found.effectiveness: EFFECTIVE - Hash chain update happens after super._update

phase5_confidence.rationale: zERC20 correctly inherits OpenZeppelin's ERC20Upgradeable. _update is called which atomically updates both balances. Custom logic (hash chain, event) happens after super._update completes.
